run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only failing workload in the cluster at query time is Deployment social-network/custom-service: it has 3 desired replicas and 3 unavailable replicas, and its three pods (custom-service-586b4dd5ff-24nkt, -9v5hm, -lqhbf) are Pending, not because of scheduling, but because the pod template contains an init container named hang-init with command `/bin/sh -c "sleep infinity"` that never terminates. Each pod shows Initialized=False with reason ContainersNotInitialized and message 'containers with incomplete status: [hang-init]', init container hang-init state=running since 04:23:48Z, and main container custom-service-main waiting with reason PodInitializing. The Deployment's last-applied-configuration annotation (revision 1) has no initContainers at all, while the live spec does, and its managedFieldsSummary records a kubectl-patch and kubectl-rollout update at 2026-11-24T04:23:47Z plus a kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt annotation at the same time; events show the previously working ReplicaSet custom-service-5c68f797 scaled from 3 to 0 and 586b4dd5ff scaled from 0 to 3 seconds later, with strategy maxUnavailable=100%/maxSurge=0% removing all old replicas before the new (init-blocked) ones could become ready. The social-network microservices were checked and showed no failure evidence: all 33 application pods were Running/Ready with 0 restarts, all Services had ready endpoint addresses, traces of nginx-web-server and its downstream services returned only HTTP 200 with no error tags in the sampled window, and the only log errors were transient MongoDB 'serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired' lines during the 04:23:37-04:23:43 startup race before MongoDB was listening. Those clean readings cover only roughly 11 seconds of trace data (04:23:50-04:24:01) because the whole environment was created at 04:23:36, so this is not a clean bill of health for the full 24-hour window.

claims.text: Deployment social-network/custom-service is at generation 3 with spec.replicas=3, status.replicas=3, status.updatedReplicas=3, status.unavailableReplicas=3, readyReplicas and availableReplicas absent (null); its pod template adds initContainers[0] name=hang-init, image=busybox:1.36, command ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep infinity"], while the kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation contains no initContainers, and the template carries annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-24T04:23:47Z.

custom-service pod custom-service-586b4dd5ff-24nkt (node sregym-worker3) has phase Pending, condition Initialized=False reason ContainersNotInitialized message 'containers with incomplete status: [hang-init]', Ready=False, init container hang-init state running (startedAt 2026-11-24T04:23:48Z) and container custom-service-main waiting with reason PodInitializing.

The same init-blocked Pending state is shown for custom-service pods custom-service-586b4dd5ff-9v5hm (node sregym-worker) and custom-service-586b4dd5ff-lqhbf (node sregym-worker2); these three are the only non-Running, non-Succeeded pods in the whole cluster, and the earlier ReplicaSet custom-service-5c68f797 pods (2np4f, 5srqf, 7tx8q) are Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

Events show the custom-service rollout sequence at 04:23:45-04:23:47Z: 'Scaled up replica set custom-service-5c68f797 from 0 to 3', three pods reaching 'Started container custom-service-main', then 'Scaled down replica set custom-service-5c68f797 from 3 to 0', a brief ReplicaSet custom-service-5d95dbc564 scaled up 0->3 and immediately back to 0, then 'Scaled up replica set custom-service-586b4dd5ff from 0 to 3' whose pods only ever start container 'hang-init'.

The managedFieldsSummary of Deployment custom-service records kubectl-client-side-apply Update at 2026-11-24T04:23:45Z, kubectl-patch Update at 2026-11-24T04:23:47Z and kubectl-rollout Update at 2026-11-24T04:23:47Z, i.e. the live pod template was changed after its initial apply.

All 26 social-network Service objects that exist (e.g. compose-post-service:9090, nginx-thrift:8080, user-service:9090, media-frontend:8081->8080) have ready Endpoints addresses and no notReadyAddresses; no Service named custom-service exists.

The social-network microservice call path was serving normally in the sampled traces: nginx-web-server /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read, /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/post/compose spans all carry http.status_code=200, downstream spans such as compose_post_server, read_user_timeline_server, get_followers_server and post_storage_read_posts_server show no error status, and zéro error spans were returned for service nginx-web-server with tag error=true.

The only application log errors in Loki were startup races between 04:23:37 and 04:23:43Z — e.g. social-graph-service 'Error in createIndexes: No suitable servers found: serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired ... social-graph-mongodb:27017' and the same pattern for user-service, url-shorten-service and user-timeline-service — plus MongoDB 'config.system.sessions does not exist' lines, all before the dependent MongoDB instances finished starting; the same services then served successful traced calls.

No node-level or scheduling cause was found: all four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) report Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure=False, and the custom-service pods have condition PodScheduled=True on three different workers, so the pods are not unschedulable.

Rejected: an application-level fault-injection setting in the social-network ConfigMaps or Deployment env/resources (e.g. injected latency/error flags, tiny CPU/memory limits) caused the problem. The per-service service-config.json is the stock configuration (timeouts 10000 ms, connections 512) with no fault flags, all application Deployments have resources {} and env null (only fqdn_suffix, COLLECTOR_ZIPKIN_HTTP_PORT), and no networkpolicies exist in social-network.

Rejected: a Service selector / Endpoint mismatch or missing ConfigMap is breaking connectivity. Every social-network Service has ready endpoint addresses, and the three transient FailedMount events in the namespace (home-timeline-redis-config, media-memcached-config, user-memcached-config: 'failed to sync configmap cache: timed out waiting for the condition') were immediately followed by 'Created container' and 'Started container' for those same pods.

Monitoring-stack churn in the observe namespace is unrelated bring-up noise: loki-0 'Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503' at 04:23:07Z, FailedMount on kube-api-access volumes of loki-chunks-cache-0 and loki-results-cache-0 at 04:22:32Z, and StatefulSet loki FailedUpdate on PVC storage-loki-0 at 04:22:30Z — all before the social-network namespace was created at 04:23:36Z.

The custom-service outage is caused by the init container hang-init (busybox, `/bin/sh -c "sleep infinity"`) added to the pod template by the kubectl-patch/rollout at 04:23:47Z: because an init container must exit before the main container starts, custom-service-main never starts and 0 of 3 replicas become ready. The pods' own status supports the mechanism, but the change record only names the manager (kubectl-patch), so who issued it and the patch body beyond annotations are unverified.

Advice: remove the hang-init init container from Deployment social-network/custom-service (or make its command terminate), i.e. roll back to the revision-1 template recorded in the last-applied-configuration annotation, and replace the maxUnavailable=100%/maxSurge=0% rollout strategy so a bad template cannot take all replicas down; then confirm all 3 pods reach Ready.

gaps: No baseline or history exists for the social-network application: Jaeger traces cover only 2026-11-24T04:23:50-04:24:01Z, Loki lines only from 04:23:37Z, and the namespace's deployments/pods were all created at 04:23:36-04:23:41Z, so pre-incident latency/error behaviour and any earlier fault cannot be compared.

Prometheus did not return application-level telemetry: traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count were not among the 735 metric names listed, and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available / pod-ready queries for namespace social-network returned no samples at 2026-11-24T04:24:04Z, so app error rates, latency trends and the custom-service replica trend could not be measured from metrics.

The change_history integration is not configured in this Run, so the actor, body and rationale of the kubectl-patch / kubectl-rollout Updates at 2026-11-24T04:23:47Z (beyond managedFieldsSummary and annotations) could not be verified, and it is unknown whether the hang-init container was ever expected to terminate.

No Service object exists for custom-service and no consumer or caller of it was observed, so whether the custom-service outage affects any user-facing social-network flow is unverified; the application microservices themselves showed no failure evidence in the sampled data.

Pod container status details for the deleted earlier ReplicaSets (custom-service-5c68f797, custom-service-5d95dbc564) beyond the events are unknown, so their template contents cannot be compared with revision 3.
next_steps: Inspect and remove/repair the hang-init init container in Deployment social-network/custom-service, then verify 3/3 pods become Ready.
Roll back custom-service to the revision-1 template recorded in kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration and set a safe rollingUpdate strategy (maxUnavailable below 100%, maxSurge above 0%).
Enable or supply change history for the cluster so the origin of the 2026-11-24T04:23:47Z kubectl-patch/kubectl-rollout can be attributed.

Re-check the social-network request path once more traffic and history exist (span metrics or http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) to exclude latency regressions that the 11-second sampled trace window cannot show.
